summary: SpectraScope is an interactive platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission, allowing users to explore infrared astronomical images, inspect observations, and visualize spectral data through an accessible interface using NASA/IPAC archive data. It aims to make astronomical data exploration easier for researchers, students, and space enthusiasts.
details: • SpectraScope: Exploring the Infrared Universe -Project Overview SpectraScope is an interactive web-based platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission. It aims to make infrared astronomical observations more accessible and easier to explore by bringing astronomical image visualization, observation inspection, and spectral information together in one place. Modern space missions collect enormous amounts of scientific data, but exploring and understanding these datasets can be challenging, particularly for students, astronomy enthusiasts, and people who are not familiar with professional astronomical analysis tools. SpectraScope addresses this challenge by providing a more accessible way to interact with astronomical observations and investigate the information they contain. -How It Works The platform allows users to search for astronomical targets by name or coordinates and explore available SPHEREx observations through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). Its current features include: - Astronomical Image Exploration: Search for targets and explore available infrared observations, including different data releases and observation details. - Image Visualization: Adjust image stretching, colour maps, and display limits to examine astronomical images in different ways. - Pixel Inspection: Explore individual image pixels and view information such as their coordinates, wavelength, surface brightness, and associated flags. - Spectral Visualization: Examine wavelength and surface-brightness information through an interactive spectral plot. - Observation Analysis: Inspect multiple available exposures and their associated measurements. -The Science Behind the Project SPHEREx is a NASA space telescope designed to survey the entire sky in near-infrared light across 102 spectral bands, covering wavelengths from approximately 0.75 to 5 micrometres. These observations provide valuable information about galaxies, stars, and other astronomical objects. SpectraScope uses the SPHEREx mission as its scientific foundation and focuses on making its observations easier to navigate, visualize, and investigate. -Who Can Benefit? SpectraScope is intended for astronomy students, researchers, educators, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in exploring infrared astronomy. By providing an interactive interface for examining astronomical observations, the project aims to encourage curiosity, support learning, and make scientific datasets less intimidating to explore. -Current Development and Future Plans SpectraScope is currently a working prototype, with several features implemented and further development planned. One of the main features I hope to introduce is an astronomical time-lapse visualization. This would allow users to select a specific region of the sky and view repeated observations from different dates as an animation, making it easier to investigate how that region changes over time. Other future improvements include expanding the available observation-analysis tools and providing more detailed scientific context for the displayed data. -Project Vision SpectraScope began with a simple question: How can we make exploring astronomical data more accessible and interactive? Inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission, the project is an attempt to bring scientific observations closer to the people who are curious about the universe. Although it is still a prototype, SpectraScope represents a foundation that can be expanded into a more comprehensive platform for astronomical exploration.
